answer: A sybil defense can work like seasoned timber viewed through a prism. New identities start as green wood: their deeds must age in public before carrying weight, so spinning up a thousand fresh shells buys no influence. When an agent makes a costly claim, independent auditors refract it like light through a prism, each checking a different facet — past work, peer endorsements, and staked resources — and only converging verdicts count. The agent's core record sits inside a walnut shell that opens gradually as facets agree, so a forger must fake time, consensus, and history at once.
